witnesses.title: Witness / Earl's programme sheet
witnesses.page:
REYES / NOTEBOOK COPY

1420 AM / NIGHT LINE

I heard a boy call about a star with a little tail, low in the south.

EARL'S PROGRAMME SHEET, copied by hand:
BOY / COMET
Caller number: blank.

EARL:
"I put the receiver down and tried the line again. Dial tone. Just a phone."

He still has not played the reel from September 1981. I have not heard that reel.

witnesses.title: Witness / The empty patrol car
witnesses.page:
REYES / NOTEBOOK COPY

HIGHWAY NORTH OF CALICHE

The deputy's car on the shoulder. Engine running, driver's door open, nobody in it. His hat was on the seat.

THE DEPUTY, back at the substation:
"I drove the loop. I came straight back."

When I mentioned the hat, he looked at the one hanging beside the door. He asked for my account on a loose sheet. This is my notebook copy.

witnesses.title: Witness / Two counts at the pasture
witnesses.page:
REYES / NOTEBOOK COPY

PASTURE SOUTH OF THE MOTEL

First count: nine cattle.
Second count: eight. A ring of flattened grass, white with frost, where the ninth stood.

THE WOMAN AT THE LAUNDROMAT:
"You counted them?"
"Write both numbers. Before you start thinking you counted wrong."

I asked if her husband found one missing the night he went out to the cattle in March 1983.
"He never said."

witnesses.title: Witness / The attendant and the payphone
witnesses.page:
REYES / NOTEBOOK COPY

MAIN STREET PAYPHONE

On the line: the control room printer. Afterwards, a bright nickel dated 1947 in the coin return.

THE ATTENDANT, shown the coin:
"That phone takes dimes."
"Keep it. I write down what goes in the till. I want it to add up."

He pushed the coin back across the sill. I kept it.
